title: When the Scaffold Stays On: AI, Practice Style, and Screening in Elite Skill Formation
abstract: arXiv:2606.06253v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Generative AI raises short-term productivity by completing tasks that learners would otherwise practice on their own. Whether this exchange erodes frontier skill depends on the mode of use: substitute-users let AI stand in for deliberate practice and fail to develop skill, while complement-users use it to accelerate skill development. For institutions that train and certify talent, the design question is not whether to allow AI but how to govern the mode of its use. We ask whether AI-prohibited evaluation gates can separate the two modes. translated_title: 当脚手架留存：人工智能、实践风格与精英技能形成中的筛选
translated_abstract: 生成式人工智能通过完成学习者原本会自行练习的任务，短期内提升了生产力。这种交换是否会侵蚀前沿技能，取决于使用模式：替代型用户让AI代替刻意练习，从而未能发展技能；而互补型用户则利用AI加速技能发展。对于培训和认证人才的机构而言，设计问题不在于是否允许AI，而在于如何规范其使用模式。我们探讨禁止AI的评估关卡能否区分这两种模式。在精英编程竞赛中，国际大学生程序设计竞赛（ICPC）和国际信息学奥林匹克（IOI）在人工监考下禁止AI，且需通过资格赛进入，而Codeforces（CF）练习则无监考且对所有人开放。从CF提交历史中，我们构建了一个AI提示签名：更多首次尝试即通过、更少尝试次数、更少调试。
tldr: 本研究通过分析精英编程竞赛中的AI使用模式，发现禁止AI的评估关卡能有效区分替代型与互补型用户，从而保护前沿技能的发展。
en_tdlr: This study analyzes AI usage patterns in elite programming contests and finds that AI-prohibited evaluation gates can effectively distinguish substitute-users from complement-users, thereby safeguarding frontier skill development.
